title: Akaunting
body:
Software overview &
accounting workflow

A practical guide to the modules, everyday transactions, reports and optional accounting apps.

FEATURE TREE   /   ACCOUNTING TREE   /   WORKED EXAMPLES
Prepared for Judibas product discussion

Research checked: 20 October 2026
PDF guide + editable Word document

Based on public official documentation. The private contents, installed apps and subscription of your Akaunting account have not been inspected. This is an independent guide, not an official Akaunting manual.

title: 01 / What the software does
body:
Akaunting brings customer billing, supplier costs, money movements and financial visibility into one business application. The cloud application is reached through app.akaunting.com. A self-hosted edition is also available. [1, 18, 19]

How to read this guide

PagesContents

5-7Sales, purchases and bank transactions
8-9Accounting records, cash/accrual and financial reports
10-12Access, settings, optional apps and integrations

Availability labels: [F] documented platform function; inclusion and limits depend on edition/plan. [A] separate app or app-dependent capability. [E] illustrative example or recommended working practice, not a claim about a particular screen.

What is not assumed

No claim is made that every feature is free, installed in your account or supported by every bank. Exact pricing, user limits and app bundles must be checked against the selected subscription. The pricing page could not be reliably retrieved during this review.

Sources: [1] Product features, [18] Cloud versus self-hosted, [19] Cloud sign-in

title: 02 / Feature tree
body:
A conceptual map of the product, rather than a literal copy of its menu. [A] marks optional or app-dependent branches.

Start with the business records; add specialist apps only when needed. Sources [1, 2, 9, 10, 16, 17].

title: 03 / Accounting workflow tree
body:
Follow the transaction from setup to payment, verification and reporting. This diagram is an explanatory synthesis of the documented workflows.

An invoice or bill and its payment are related records. Creating one does not mean the other has happened. Sources [3-12]; controls in step 7 are recommendations [E].

title: 04 / Sales: from invoice to receipt
body:
Customers and invoices [F]

Create a customer, choose the invoice date and reference, then add products or services with descriptions, quantities and rates. Apply configured taxes and eligible line or overall discounts. Notes, categories and attachments provide context. Save and send the invoice through the available delivery options. [3]

Receiving money [F]

Record payment against the invoice using the actual receipt date, payment account and method. Payments can be full or partial. A remaining balance is still owed by the customer; an invoice should not be treated as fully settled merely because it was sent. [4]

RecordPurposeExample [E]
CustomerWho is buyingCedar Retail
InvoiceWhat they oweServices: Rs 100,000
Payment / receiptMoney actually receivedRs 60,000 into bank
Outstanding balanceAmount still to collectRs 40,000
Practical check [E]: when a bank receipt already exists, connect it to the invoice rather than recording the same receipt twice.

Related capabilities

The client portal exposes customer-facing records. Recurring documents support repeat billing. Estimates are a separate capability whose app/plan availability should be checked. [1, 17]

Sources: [3] Creating an invoice, [4] Invoice payments, [1] Product features, [17] Apps and integrations

title: 05 / Purchases: bills and expenses
body:
Supplier bills [F]

A bill records a supplier obligation. Choose the vendor and document date, enter the bill reference, add items, prices and applicable taxes or discounts, and attach supporting evidence. Categories and notes help explain the cost. [5]

Payment versus obligation [F]

Record the supplier payment against the bill, including the payment account, amount and date. Partial payments leave an unpaid balance. Direct expenses can instead represent spending that is recorded without a separate supplier bill. [6, 7]

SituationRecord to considerControl [E]
Supplier allows payment laterBill, followed by paymentKeep due date and unpaid amount visible
Expense paid immediatelyDirect expense or paid billDo not record both for one cost
Part-payment to supplierPayment against existing billCheck the remaining balance
Regular rent or service chargeRecurring bill where availableReview amount before paying

Worked example [E]

A supplier bill is Rs 30,000. The business pays Rs 20,000 from its bank account. The payment reduces the amount owed to Rs 10,000. The bill total remains Rs 30,000; the payment is not another purchase.

Sources: [5] Creating a bill, [6] Bill payments, [7] Bank transactions

title: 06 / Banking and money movements
body:
Accounts and transactions [F]

Cash and bank accounts identify where money is held. Income and expense transactions record the date, method, account, amount, category and reference. Existing money movements may be connected to matching invoices or bills, including partial-payment situations. [1, 7]

MovementPlain-language meaningRecording check [E]
Income receiptMoney coming into an accountIdentify the customer or reason
Expense paymentMoney leaving an accountIdentify the supplier or reason
Account transferMoney moved between own accountsDo not treat the transfer as a new sale
Opening balanceMoney already held at the starting dateVerify against the migration cutoff

Bank feeds [A]

The Bank Feeds app can synchronize transactions from supported institutions. The official help page lists the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, UK and EU. Do not assume Pakistani bank connectivity; confirm the specific institution and current provider coverage. Manual transaction entry remains a separate workflow. [8]

Reconciliation [E]

Compare the bank statement with recorded money movements. Investigate duplicates, missing fees, wrong dates and incorrect amounts before relying on cash balances. A feed imports information; it does not remove the need for review.

Sources: [1] Product features, [7] Bank transactions, [8] Bank feeds

title: 07 / The accounting layer
body:
Double-entry is a separate capability [A]

The Chart of Accounts feature requires the Double-Entry app. Accounts can have a code, classification and parent account. The main classifications cover assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses. The app adds ledger-oriented accounting, including journal and statement capabilities. [9, 10]

Account familyWhat it representsIllustrative account [E]
AssetsResources the business ownsBank, customer receivables
LiabilitiesAmounts the business owesSupplier payables
EquityOwner interest in the businessOwner capital
IncomeValue earned by the businessService revenue
ExpensesCosts incurredRent, office supplies

Cash versus accrual [F]

Akaunting documents accrual-based accounting and a cash option in reports. Accrual looks at when income is earned or costs are incurred; cash looks at receipt and payment timing. Results can differ even for the same period. Confirm the basis selected before comparing reports. [11]

Illustration [E]: invoice Rs 100,000; receipt Rs 60,000. Ignoring taxes and other adjustments, the earned amount and cash received are different. A debit/credit example appears on page 13.

Sources: [9] Chart of accounts, [10] Double-Entry app, [11] Cash versus accrual

title: 08 / Reports: what each answers
body:
Report names appear in the official catalogue, but their availability depends on the installed apps and plan. A catalogue entry alone does not mean it is included in the basic application. [12]

Report / viewQuestion it answersAvailability note
Income summaryWhere did recorded income come from?Documented reporting
Expense summaryWhere are recorded costs concentrated?Documented reporting
Income versus expenseHow do the two totals compare?Documented reporting
Tax summaryWhat tax amounts were recorded?Configuration and report dependent
Customer statementWhat activity belongs to this customer?Check plan/report availability
Profit and lossWhat is the accounting result for a period?Check basis and accounting app
Balance sheetWhat are assets, liabilities and equity?Double-Entry related [A]
Trial balanceWhat are debit/credit balances by account?Double-Entry related [A]
General ledgerWhat entries make up account balances?Double-Entry related [A]
Cash flow statementHow did cash change across activities?Check app/report availability

Read reports consistently [E]

Use the same company, reporting dates, currency treatment and cash/accrual basis. Trace an unexpected total back to its underlying records. A tax summary is not proof that a tax return has been filed or accepted.

Sources: [12] Reports catalogue, [10] Double-Entry app, [11] Cash versus accrual

title: 09 / Users, companies and access
body:
Documented roles include Accountant, Customer, Employee and Manager, with Admin also listed for the self-hosted edition. The cloud and self-hosted role models are not identical. The help page states that on-premise role management requires the Roles & Permissions app. [13]

Recommended access design [E]

PersonAppropriate working scopeAvoid granting automatically
Business ownerOversight of permitted companiesUnrestricted access to unrelated entities
AccountantFinancial records and accounting reportsInfrastructure administration without need
Accounts operatorPrepare invoices, bills and receiptsUncontrolled accounting adjustments
ManagerRelevant oversight and approved actionsFull access merely because of job title
EmployeeTheir permitted employee workflowsWhole-company financial information
CustomerTheir own portal recordsOther customers or internal records

Company separation [F / E]

Akaunting supports multiple businesses and company assignments. Treat company selection as a data boundary. Before rollout, test whether each role can view, create, edit, delete and export the intended records. The matrix above is a recommended policy, not a reproduction of Akaunting defaults.

Sources: [13] Roles and permissions, [1] Product features

title: 10 / Setup and configuration
body:
Business setup checklist [E]

  • Choose cloud or self-hosting and identify the accountable administrator.
  • Create the business profile and confirm the default currency and reporting dates.
  • Set invoice identity, numbering conventions and customer-facing text.
  • Add cash/bank accounts and agree opening balances at a single cutoff date.
  • Prepare customer, vendor and product/service lists.
  • Configure named tax rates and review how they apply to transactions.
  • Map categories; add ledger accounts if Double-Entry is installed.
  • Assign company access and permitted roles before inviting the wider team.

Tax configuration [F]

Akaunting documents creation and management of tax rates. Configure the intended rate and type before applying them to items or documents. Do not assume that choosing a tax label implements every local reporting or filing rule. [14]

Products and services [F / A]

Items provide reusable names, descriptions and prices for billing and purchasing. Stock quantities, warehouses and inventory operations belong to the Inventory app scope; a basic item list is not a full stock-control system. [15, 16]

Illustration only: all rupee amounts in this guide are examples. No statutory tax percentage, local filing integration or regulatory compliance has been assumed.

Sources: [14] Tax rates, [15] Products and services, [16] Inventory app, [2] Documentation index

title: 11 / Optional apps and deployment
body:
Akaunting distinguishes native feature apps from third-party integrations. Installing or purchasing an app can extend the menus and workflow. These extensions should be scoped separately from everyday invoicing and bill entry. [17]

App area [A]Business purposeWhat to verify
Double-EntryAccounts, journals and financial statementsAvailability, account mappings and opening entries
InventoryWarehouses, variants and stock operationsQuantity rules and accounting integration
Estimates / quotesProposals before invoicingConversion and document behaviour
Payroll / employeesPay calendars and payslipsCountry-specific suitability
Projects / CRMProject work and customer pipelineOverlap with existing business systems
Expense claimsEmployee claim and approval workflowsApproval scope and payment handling
Payment integrationsOnline collectionProvider coverage, fees and settlement
Bank FeedsBank transaction synchronizationSupported country and institution

Cloud or self-hosted?

Cloud uses Akaunting-hosted infrastructure; self-hosting places the application on infrastructure you operate. For self-hosting, plan for deployment, updates, restore testing and maintenance. Check the current subscription and app terms for either route rather than relying on broad free-software marketing. [18]

Sources: [17] Apps and integrations, [16] Inventory app, [10] Double-Entry app, [8] Bank feeds, [18] Cloud versus self-hosted

title: 12 / One complete accounting example
body:
Illustrative double-entry explanation [E]. Assumes the Double-Entry capability, accrual accounting, no tax, one currency and no inventory.

EventBusiness recordIllustrative accounting effect
1. Invoice customer Rs 100,000Customer invoiceDebit receivables 100,000; credit revenue 100,000
2. Receive Rs 60,000Payment linked to invoiceDebit bank 60,000; credit receivables 60,000
3. Supplier bill Rs 30,000Expense billDebit expense 30,000; credit payables 30,000
4. Pay supplier Rs 20,000Payment linked to billDebit payables 20,000; credit bank 20,000

Result after these four events

MeasureAmountMeaning
Revenue earnedRs 100,000Does not mean all cash was received
Expense incurredRs 30,000Does not mean all cash was paid
Illustrative profitRs 70,000100,000 less 30,000
Net bank movementRs 40,000 increase60,000 received less 20,000 paid
Customer balanceRs 40,000 receivableStill to collect
Supplier balanceRs 10,000 payableStill to pay
Profit and cash movement differ. The invoice, receipt, bill and payment each describe a different part of the same business activity. This example explains the concepts; it is not a guarantee of automatic posting under every configuration.

Sources: [11] Cash versus accrual, [9] Chart of accounts, [10] Double-Entry app

title: 13 / Operating checklist and glossary
body:
Recommended routine [E]

WhenReview
DailyEnter new documents; record receipts/payments; attach evidence; check overdue items.
WeeklyMatch bank movements; resolve duplicate or unconnected records; review customer/supplier balances.
MonthlyReconcile accounts; check cash/accrual basis; review statements and unusual postings; retain exports.
When access changesRemove unnecessary company permissions and verify customer/employee isolation.
Before an app or major updateConfirm compatibility, test critical workflows and check the recovery plan.

Plain-language glossary

TermMeaning
InvoiceDocument requesting customer payment.
BillSupplier document recording what the business owes.
Receivable / payableAmount to collect / amount to pay.
Payment accountThe cash or bank account used for a money movement.
Category / ledger accountA business grouping / a formal accounting classification. They are not interchangeable.
Journal / ledgerBalanced accounting entry / history grouped by account.
ReconciliationComparing recorded activity with external evidence, usually a statement.
Accrual / cash basisRecognition by earning/incurring / recognition by receiving/paying.

Concept definitions and routines are explanatory material, not a claim that every control has a dedicated Akaunting screen.
